query: Which audio codecs and bitrates best balance intelligibility and file-size for low-bandwidth mobile audio tasks in low-resource school contexts, under realistic handset/connectivity conditions?

response.query: Which audio codecs and bitrates best balance intelligibility and file-size for low-bandwidth mobile audio tasks in low-resource school contexts, under realistic handset/connectivity conditions?
response.answer: For low-bandwidth mobile audio tasks, AAC codec at 64 kbps balances intelligibility and file size well. MP3 at 128 kbps is also effective. Higher bitrates may not be necessary for most educational content.

results.title: What are the cons of MP3s when it comes to audio quality?
results.content: TLDR: If your music collection is CD-based, rip at 16-bit/44kHz into FLAC or ALAC format. If you have a choice of music at 320kbs vs. 16/44, take 16/44.
